title: Gateway requests return errors
briefing: An aggregate gateway alert has fired. Determine which diagnostic would isolate the failing traffic.

actions.label: Compare rollout cohorts
actions.criteria: Use when errors appear during a staged gateway change and cohort timing could distinguish a regression.
actions.instructions: Compare error rates for the previous and current gateway deployment cohorts.

actions.label: Inspect the selected backend pool
actions.criteria: Use when failing requests are routed to a pool whose traffic assignment conflicts with the configuration.
actions.instructions: Compare the actual backend pool in failed traces with the expected pool for those requests.

actions.label: Inspect gateway transport errors
actions.criteria: Use when failures appear before routing or cluster around a TLS or connection error.
actions.instructions: Compare handshake and connection errors across gateway regions and backend pools.

fallback: Collect a failed gateway trace with its deployment cohort and backend selection.

events.text: The gateway 5xx rate rose from 0.2% to 3.5% during a staged rollout. Both gateway versions are currently serving traffic, and the aggregate alert has no cohort breakdown.
Staged gateway release edge-104 started at 15:59 UTC and reached 15% traffic at 16:02. The prior gateway continues to handle the remaining requests.
The new rollout must send EU merchant requests to pool blue. Pool amber is configured for APAC merchants.
Failed requests share region=EU, deployment=edge-104, and backend=amber.

debrief.summary: The staged gateway release selected the APAC pool for EU merchant requests. Comparing the observed pool to the routing registry made the mismatch actionable.
lessons: Cohort comparisons help narrow a deploy-related failure.
An opaque pool label becomes diagnostic when paired with the routing configuration.
